content.value_statement: Japanese salary withholding varies with payment year, eligible dependents, and pay after social insurance. This skill calculates local formula-based estimates and explains differences from printed tax tables.
actual_capabilities: Estimate monthly column A income-tax withholding from salary after social insurance and eligible dependent counts.
Apply separate bundled deduction constants for 2026 and 2027 payment years.
Show employment-income deductions, dependent deductions, basic deductions, taxable income, and estimated withholding.
Apply deduction rounding and round calculated withholding to the nearest 10 yen.
Explain documented differences between formula estimates and printed monthly tax tables.
Calculate locally using Python standard-library modules and reject unsupported years or negative inputs.
limitations: Only 2026 and 2027 are supported; the calculator defaults to 2026 and does not automatically update tax rules.
Inputs must be integer yen after social insurance and eligible dependent counts; the skill does not determine eligibility.
Column B, bonuses, daily tables, retirement pay, resident tax, annual returns, and year-end adjustment calculations are excluded.
Results are estimates and may differ from printed tables or employer withholding; they do not calculate total take-home pay.

use_cases.title: Check a monthly payslip estimate
use_cases.description: Estimate withholding from salary after social insurance and compare the result with employer deductions.

use_cases.title: Compare payment-year assumptions
use_cases.description: Compare 2026 and 2027 formula estimates for identical salary and dependent inputs before discussing payroll differences.

use_cases.title: Explain deduction calculations
use_cases.description: Show a worked deduction breakdown and explain why formula estimates can differ from monthly tax-table amounts.

prompt_templates.title: Get a basic estimate
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate my 2026 monthly withholding for 175,000 yen after social insurance and two eligible dependents. State the tax-table limitation.

prompt_templates.title: Review the deduction breakdown
prompt_templates.prompt: For [year], estimate withholding on [salary] yen after social insurance with [dependents] eligible dependents. Show each deduction and the rounding.

prompt_templates.title: Compare supported years
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare 2026 and 2027 monthly withholding estimates for 300,000 yen after social insurance and zero eligible dependents. Identify changed deductions and estimate differences.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a payroll discrepancy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [year] withholding for [salary] yen after social insurance, [dependents] eligible dependents, and employer withholding of [amount] yen. Explain possible formula-versus-table differences without assuming employer error.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: reconcile an estimate with a payslip.

output_examples.input: Estimate 2026 withholding for 175,000 yen after social insurance and two eligible dependents.
output: Employment-income deduction: 59,167 yen. Dependent deduction: 63,334 yen. Basic deduction: 48,334 yen.
Taxable monthly income: 4,165 yen. Estimated withholding: 210 yen.
The documented printed-table amount is 250 yen. The formula estimate is not a guaranteed payroll amount.

output_examples.input: Estimate 2027 withholding for 177,000 yen after social insurance and two eligible dependents.
output: Employment-income deduction: 59,767 yen. Dependent deduction: 63,334 yen. Basic deduction: 51,667 yen.
Taxable monthly income: 2,232 yen. Estimated withholding: 110 yen.
The documented printed-table amount is 150 yen. Confirm actual withholding with the employer or applicable tax table.

best_practices: Use salary after social insurance deductions, not gross salary or total take-home pay.
Specify the payment year explicitly and confirm the eligible dependent count before calculating.
Compare estimates with the applicable official table and employer payslip before making payroll decisions.
anti_patterns: Entering gross salary as salary after social insurance.
Treating formula estimates as exact tax-table values or final annual tax liabilities.
Using the default 2026 year for other payment years or applying the calculator to bonuses and column B.

faq.question: Which payment years are supported?
faq.answer: The calculator supports 2026 and 2027 only. It defaults to 2026, so specify the payment year explicitly.

faq.question: Which salary amount should I enter?
faq.answer: Enter monthly salary after social insurance deductions as integer yen. Do not enter gross salary or final take-home pay.

faq.question: How should I count dependents?
faq.answer: Use withholding-eligible spouse and relative counts, including applicable disability or single-parent adjustments. Confirm eligibility separately; the calculator does not assess it.

faq.question: Why can the result differ from my payslip?
faq.answer: The formula and printed monthly tables can produce different amounts. Employer methods, payment year, and dependent counts also affect withholding.

faq.question: Does calculation require network access?
faq.answer: No. The Python calculator uses bundled constants and standard-library modules locally. Official PDF links provide references rather than automatic updates.

faq.question: Can it calculate bonuses or annual tax?
faq.answer: No. It covers monthly column A withholding estimates only, not bonuses, column B, resident tax, year-end adjustments, or annual returns.
